classification.difficultyReason: Interpret supplied gradients and intercepts using axis units and insert them into linear equations; the hardest case requires recognising population units as thousands and explaining a negative rate.

content.prompt: Identify what the gradient and $y$-intercepts of these graphs represent, then write the equation.

spec.description: Unscaled rising cost–time graph; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid. Coordinate units are internal construction values and are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible; interpretation and equation responses are hidden.

answer.worked: The cost increases by $\$0.50$ for each additional hour.
At $t=0$, the cost is $\$2$. This is the initial cost.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $0.5$ and intercept $2$ gives
$$C=0.5t+2.$$

spec.description: Unscaled descending fuel–distance graph terminating on the horizontal axis; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.short: Fuel decreases by 0.8 L per kilometre.
answer.worked: The gradient is $-0.8$ litres per kilometre, so the fuel remaining decreases by 0.8 L for each kilometre travelled.
At $d=0$, there are 15 L of fuel. This is the initial fuel volume.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $-0.8$ and intercept $15$ gives
$$f=-0.8d+15.$$

spec.description: Unscaled rising height–time graph with a positive intercept; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.short: Height increases by 2.5 cm per month.
answer.worked: The height increases by 2.5 cm for each additional month.
At $t=0$, the height is 50 cm. This is the initial height.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $2.5$ and intercept $50$ gives
$$h=2.5t+50.$$

spec.description: Unscaled rising Fahrenheit–Celsius graph with a positive intercept; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.worked: For each $1^\circ\mathrm{C}$ increase in Celsius temperature, Fahrenheit temperature increases by $1.8^\circ\mathrm{F}$.
When $C=0$, $F=32$, so $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ corresponds to $32^\circ\mathrm{F}$.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $1.8$ and intercept $32$ gives
$$F=1.8C+32.$$

spec.description: Unscaled rising cost–distance graph; arrowed axes, no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.short: Cost increases by 3 dollars per kilometre.
answer.worked: The cost increases by $\$3$ for each additional kilometre.
At $d=0$, the cost is $\$5$. This is the initial cost.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $3$ and intercept $5$ gives

spec.description: Unscaled descending height–time graph ending above the horizontal axis; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.short: Height decreases by 10 mm per hour.
answer.worked: The gradient is $-10$ millimetres per hour, so the height decreases by 10 mm each hour.
At $t=0$, the height is 80 mm. This is the initial height.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $-10$ and intercept $80$ gives
$$h=-10t+80.$$

spec.description: Unscaled rising pay–sales graph with a positive intercept; arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.worked: Pay increases by $\$0.10$ for each additional dollar of sales.

answer.short: $\$300$ pay for $\$0$ sales (initial pay, or retainer).
answer.worked: At $s=0$, pay is $\$300$. This is the initial pay, or retainer.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $0.1$ and intercept $300$ gives
$$P=0.1s+300.$$

spec.description: Unscaled gently descending population–time graph ending above the horizontal axis; population is measured in thousands. Arrowed axes, no ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: P = -2t + 50, where P is population in thousands
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied unscaled model is visible.

answer.short: Population decreases by 2000 people per year.
answer.worked: Population is measured in thousands. A gradient of $-2$ means a decrease of $2\times1000=2000$ people each year.
At $t=0$, the population is 50 thousand, or 50 000 people. This is the initial population.

Using $y=mx+c$ with gradient $-2$ and intercept $50$ gives
$$P=-2t+50,$$
where $P$ is population in thousands and $t$ is time in years.
